record.original_question: Develop criteria for dynamic stability and instability of equilibria in nonlinear elasticity, including which notions of local minimizer ensure Lyapunov or asymptotic stability and how instability can be justified.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Develop criteria for the dynamic stability and instability of equilibria.
it is not clear which kinds of local minimizers are needed to ensure dynamical stability.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hyperelastic body occupying a bounded reference domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ with Lipschitz boundary, governed by a stored-energy function $W:\Omega\times M^{3\times 3}_+\to\mathbb{R}$ (with $M^{3\times 3}_+$ the $3\times 3$ matrices of positive determinant). The total elastic energy of a deformation $y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is
$$E(y)=\int_\Omega W(x,\nabla y(x))\,dx,$$
subject to suitable boundary conditions (e.g. $y=\bar y$ on a part $\partial\Omega_1$ of $\partial\Omega$ and prescribed traction or zero traction on the remainder). The dynamic equations of motion are
$$\rho\, y_{tt} = \operatorname{Div}\bigl(D_F W(x,\nabla y)\bigr) + b(x,t),\qquad x\in\Omega,\; t>0,$$
together with the chosen boundary conditions and initial data $y(\cdot,0)=y_0$, $y_t(\cdot,0)=y_1$. Assume $W$ is polyconvex and satisfies natural growth and frame-indifference hypotheses sufficient for existence of equilibria as minimizers of $E$.

An equilibrium $\bar y$ (a critical point of $E$) is called Lyapunov stable for the dynamic equations if for every neighborhood $U$ of $(\bar y,0)$ in a chosen function-space topology there exists a neighborhood $V\subset U$ such that every weak solution $(y(\cdot,t),y_t(\cdot,t))$ with $(y_0,y_1)\in V$ remains in $U$ for all $t\ge 0$; asymptotically stable if in addition $(y(\cdot,t),y_t(\cdot,t))\to(\bar y,0)$ as $t\to\infty$. Recall a deformation $\bar y$ is a local minimizer of $E$ in a topology $\tau$ if $E(\bar y)\le E(y)$ for all admissible $y$ in some $\tau$-neighborhood of $\bar y$.

Problem. Develop rigorous criteria for the dynamic stability and instability of equilibria in nonlinear elasticity. In particular:
(a) Identify which notions of local minimizer of $E$ (e.g. strong $L^\infty$ local minimizers, $W^{1,p}$ local minimizers for various $p$, quasiconvex-at-the-boundary local minimizers) suffice to imply Lyapunov, respectively asymptotic, stability of the corresponding equilibrium for the dynamic equations above.
(b) Provide verifiable conditions on $W$ and $\bar y$ under which a non-minimizing equilibrium (or a local minimizer that fails some appropriate quasiconvexity condition) is dynamically unstable, with a rigorous justification of the instability.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Problem 14 in J. M. Ball's well-known list of open problems in nonlinear elasticity, widely regarded as still open. Although there are partial results in special settings (e.g. for one-dimensional models, viscoelastic regularizations, or under strong convexity assumptions), no general criterion linking local minimality notions to dynamic Lyapunov/asymptotic stability in 3D nonlinear elasticity is known, and the question of rigorously establishing instability of non-minimizing equilibria remains unresolved.
